items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: whenever I couldn't get Spurgeon I'd used Bostic... I still liked Spurgeon better as a band man

ctx.x: Where was it held, what ballroom?

It was the ballroom right there on the points, Rosonia. Jones told me, I'll tell you what, Smiling Billy is a long way from Florida, he comes once a year, but he said I'll have you in here a lot of times, and I told him okay. But I told him then, come back again, I think I'll have a different size band, a little larger.

So I went on back then, when we did go back in Tulsa, we played those dates-- what's his name--Dorsey--had several dates and we played around and went back and Spurgeon was still going to school down in Xavier and I never would encourage him to stop school and I think Bostic had Scott around, Earl Bostic, and whenever I couldn't get Spurgeon I'd used

items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: Luther West and Spurgeons and of course (inaudible)... I was standing tenor man

ctx.x: I think people might not understand, it was revolutionary, for a white guy to be with a black band; that was a big thing.

I told him right then you can say you're the manager or anything and he said I understand, and he was a very fine fellow and a good musician and the only thing after he finally left the band, Spurgeons said, I'll tell you one thing--
(Side B of Tape 1 ended at this point. Transcript will continue with Tape 2.)

items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: Rene has just about made up his mind that he's going to go on back to Tulsa with you to join this band.

ctx.x: One or the other. He's from Tulsa too. He came here and West, they weren't exactly the same classmates, very close, but West went to Xavier in New Orleans.
By the way, so Luther would play with you just intermittently and go back to school?
